[b]Concord[/b]

They agreed. They couldn't defeat the imperial might of Vespurias as mere bands of misfits trying to make petty shamat-like warlordships just for Vespurians to do their time honoured tradition of drone strikes and carpet bombing then to the stone age, now with pyromancers on their side working as one man artillery units.

They wanted to win, not die. And the Empire won't let them win. And they can't die. The Tree Forbids It. So they'll have to win, and for that they'll fight, but firstly, agree, they cannot do this disunited. Hells take them, they will not relent, they will not stop, they will not cease until order has been revoked, and they can built their own world atop the ashes, fight for the right to be at the top, but first, they must slay the beast at the top.

Dragons. Liches. Vampires. Beasts. Archmages. Giants. Demons. Monsters.

They must coalesce into a coalition of great proportions. And destroy those who would refuse. For in the battle to be the greatest, there can be no remorse for dogmatism. For only those who win get to live, breathe, enjoy and write the day that is tomorrow. Over five hundred thousand of these forces have begun coordination, with five hundred thousand more in proposition to align.

The Imperials have acted accordingly. They've rearranged priorities, bounties have increased. The countryside has become too dangerous. Citizens are being given online and radio explanations, 24/7, on how to combat, how to survive, how to heal, how to lead, and how to win against these bastards.

The Dark Horde, dubbed after the hunnic germanic hordes they used to fight against, the enemy has been labelled, shown, painted, marked, and priced. Weapons and means are being distributed. The DYE-fication of mass monster slaughter that is not wearing the Vespurian banner or sigil.

[b]Congregation[/b]

They assembled. The first original five hundred thousand, with weapons both modern and magical. Where? [b][i]Hyperion[/i][/b]. The Imperial Capital. In the Imperial Heartland. The City of Cities. The Heart of the Empire. The Heart of [i]Vespurias[/i]. One could've said Hearth City, Avernus Citadel, or Kingsmount Capitol itself, and nobody would be surprised.

But Hyperion? The Hyperion? Our Hyperion? It baffled even the most radical and insane of generals. Hyperion had carpet giant walls taller than some buildings, layered, it was shielded magically, and the White Tree, or more aptly lately, the Golden Tree, was shining like a second sun enough to illuminate the fields beyond.

Fields now filled to the brim with the first half of the Dark Horde. Five Hundred Thousand. On every entry and choke points of the walls. A force wielding unimaginable manpower, taking advantage of a busy crown, nascent, whilst it's licking its wounds between fights, trying to pick them apart separately before going for the kill.

[b]Conquest[/b]

They attacked.

And in their desperation, made enemies of everything they befouled.

The countryside and forestry became their refuge, as they appropriated ruins of old castles or abandoned towns.

As their main host sieged out the largest city in the world, the rest of the uncertain or unworthy forces of the horde tried in their vanity to ravage to plunder and ransack the Empire, mealpiece. But the towns and villages of Vespurians were not so easy to threaten with impunity.

Seeing the threat, towns would align and coalition with eachother to forge militia forces to drive out the raiders, heavy gunfire and ingenuity making deterrents across the land. Trucks used for quick attacks and to ram enemies. Rooftops becoming high spots for death from above thanks to those sniping enemies from afar.

The Emperor, already in full detest of the title, and in yearning for meaning more beyond sitting there a symbol propped up by others, and with full executive powers he realised nobody would contest it seems, began ordering a more radical offensive approach to the Arcane Crisis.

[quote=thep;60621167][b]THEP intervenes[/b]
The rapid escalation of events in Vespurias would soon catch the attention of the THEP security council. One of the alliances own members had fallen to dark magic not seen on a scale this size for centuries. As such, the alliance knew that the response had to be of equal size to combat the growing threat. With intel from Vespurias delegations, the Security Councils military command would form a hasty strategy to counter this international crisis.

The first thing on the agenda would be to prevent the spread of magic, and the horrific creatures that became of it, outside of Vespurias. THEP would seek to establish a total naval blockade of Vespurias, firing upon ghastly beings that lurked below, or war criminals fleeing from the scene. However, THEP also knew that aid needed to get in and civilians needed to get out, so the fleets would form entrance points in the blockade, a sort of border crossing between the chaos of Vespurias and the outside world. These border crossings would be administered by THEP to allow international aid, relief and mercenaries in, whilst catching loose criminals and stopping the spread of magic.

The THEP military command would issue notices and orders to the nations of the security council, asking for their help in the immense operation, as they knew that a feat of this size would require the full force available to THEP.

Hydronia would deploy several naval fleets to the scene, despite the fact that their military would still be recovering from the THEP-EDU war. The following would be sent to the area:
[list]
1x aircraft carrier (+helicopters and jets to survey the situation from above)
75x patrol boats
4x destroyers
15x corvettes
2x minelayers
1x amphibious landing craft
3x submarines
[/list]
Hydronia knew that sending this many ships into battle would be a risky move, but the risk would be worth it to save the people of Vespurias from this living nightmare.

The event in Vespurias has also the Bobian Royal Navy to mobilise. It has been preparing for the past few months, in conjunction with the THEP military command to bombard the shores of Vespuria with artillery and guns to destroy as many demons and creatures living there, but first we have to evacuate and clear out the cities of people to safe areas. So initially 10 ships will be sent out to Vespuria to land on the beaches and deploy 20 PT-3's also known as The Pyramid Type 3 per ship. The first ship will land and deploy all 20 vehicles onto the coast, all of which will drive forwards and make a circle to protect the area where the next 10 ships will land and release there vehicles all of which will fall in behind the ones at the front once all the ships have gone the vehicles will move forwards creating a much larger ring of "Pyramids". This will then become Bobian Deployment 1. This will be repeated a further 2 times along the coast to form a protected military base. This will then be filled with soldiers, buildings and more conventional Military vehicles such as Tanks and Armoured Vehicles.

Whilst these measures from the Hydronians and the Bobians would allow for containment of the mainland, a battle had already begun in the Baliwick sea. The assembled THEP blockade fleet would delegate a handful of reconnaissance ships, escorted by missile-carrying corvettes, to observe the unfolding battle and report back to the THEP military command so that a further plan can be formulated and executed.

Meanwhile, on the diplomatic side of things, THEP has called upon its partner members to assist the humanitarian and peacekeeping efforts of the operation. THEP will need all the assistance it can get to prevent the fall of Vespurias and its people.

An inquiry about how Nordiheim may best be of aid have been sendt to the THEP security council aswell as how to best organize it according to THEPs current, and future, movements and mission objectives.

The council of Nordiheim is also potentialy willing to send a navy task force to aid aswell if this is desired by the THEP security council.[/quote][quote=western_view;60625937]Western View will send humanitarian aid ASAP, but it may be delayed due to the Guhui'Bernardio blockade[/quote]

[/quote]

[b]Battle of Balwick[/b]

How many warships rest at the bottom of the Balwick Sea? The White Sea? The White Bay? The White Strait?

Apparently enough for a full imperial naval operation, if one doesn't count the submarine battle going underneath against paranormal megafauna in the form of sea monsters thought very much dead, extinct, or at least asleep for a long while.

The Vespurian navy was already making an effort containing the beasts to not get out of Vespurian waters. But the rising wreckages of ships, warships rising from the waters full of rotten wood or rusting metal coming up and out of the stormy waters.

And attacking.

In general, this was an utter nuisance. The air force was split across the entirety of mainland Vespurias AND then their waters. Possibly the largest military operation since the 20th century's early wars. Then the Pact came. Thanks were sent to the entire Pact, such as Nordiheim and Western View.

Bobbians and Hydronians chiefly. An aid that would not soon be forgotten. They were hailed into the great sea battles ongoing as the Vespurian Navy was trying to desperately fight a wack-a-mole sort of battle against undead ghost warships hellbent on firing on anything out of confusion.

It didn't help that Albany, Llyndorra, and Montfleur had basically filled the White Sea and therefore the White Bay so full of sunken ships over the last thousand years to make it an issue. The admiralty that once enjoyed the classic Man of Wars style of the golden age now loathed them with a burning fire.

The Navy helped in getting the Pact forces to land, if anything, safer, in Misty Isle, and then, Kingsmount and Averne. The Pact blockade of this grand fleet of death gave the Vespurians a breathing room that permitted them to fully engage the enemy, and let those who are trying to slip away to be handled by the Pact forces.

The Pyramids were very strange.

Even the Vespurians had to pause a bit to see what they were witnessing before assessing anything capable of going against a fifteen feet tall demon that flies and craps fire is good enough for them. The coastline militias of the eastern coast would quickly join on the Bobbian Deployments, which the Vespurians would nickname the Bobbian Defenders.

Meanwhile airborne enemies became befuddled. From dragons to harpies to flying eyeballs with bat wings. With the additional aid from the Pact, more of the official forces were relieved to be sent to Hyperion, now under attack, to counter offence the Dark Horde that waits at the gates.

[quote=norrhollow;60441981][b]What will the shareholders say?[/b]

Xavier Almstedt walked through the empty hallways of his corporate offices. Just hours ago, these marbled tiles clicked loudly beneath the sound of a hundred or feet shifting in and out of the offices and rooms therein. He had just finished yet another troublesome meeting of shareholders, supposedly meant to take place online. Nearly a tenth of visitors visiting Almstedt Tower anyways, mostly older gentlemen and irate investors. Vespuria was in a crisis. The White Tree, the iconic symbol of magical concentration in Vespuria, had mysteriously erupted for reasons which were still not clear to most news reports. The dead walk the earth and latent energy now permeated the thickening air.

And so, a meeting had been called by the shareholders of Almstedt Corporation, not to discuss any specific evacuation measures, but to receive assurances from Xavier that their investments were going to be safe and sound.

Because of the way that Almstedt Corporation was structured, it effectively permeated all aspects of life in the State of Norrhollow, one of Vespuria's wealthiest and most well-developed states. Placed overlooking the White Strait and Austmark Island, it was well-insulated from whatever disaster was happening further inland, though that wasn't to say things were fine and dandy. Governor Eske Fjällstra, who had already been considered maddened before the eruption, now seemed to stare out into open space muttering indecipherable tongue, while all around Stormhaven the Thrømm and Norrics walked with a dazed, almost nauseous expression, like they had been forcefully fed with something unpleasant.

Something needed to be done, for the sake of Almstedt Corporation's revenue. Oh, and they could probably help a few people too.

What had to be understood about Almstedt Corporation is that it was a holding company, and within its immense asset profile were several highly profitable private entities that over the years have been hard at work in prosecuting human suffering to the highest bidder. SummitONE was the most obvious one, but also MROS Dynamics in Sikirsk, Pax International wreaking havoc in Astanir, SummitONE Seagates in Sal-Baliz, never mind their funding vehicles like Porthwaite Opportunities, Quad Capital, and Dearborn Bank. And each subdivision had separate owners, concealed beyond layers of parent shell companies and fictitious boards of directors.

Xavier himself wasn't even technically Chairman of his own company, instead officially calling himself a COO, with all executive power nominally in the hands of his elder sister, Honor. Therefore, what he chooses to do now, which may define the fate of Vespertine society in the next ten or so years, he can endeavor to do no matter the cost, with the full knowledge that in the event of disaster, others will take the fall for him. With the board of directors of Almstedt Corporation anxious to resolve the crisis as quickly as possible, Xavier would authorize SummitONE to begin yet another operation.

[b]Separate Group of Forces[/b]

The three largest military forces in Norrhollow were the Norrhollow State Reserve, the Crisis Action Under Special Emergencies (CAUSE), and SummitONE itself. Typically, these various military formations acted subordinate to the wider Vespertine military framework. However, things were no longer business as usual. With Governor Fjällstra currently indisposed, Xavier would successfully persuade his sister Honor Almstedt to take up the mantle of acting governor of Norrhollow, effectively integrating the Almstedt family into the state apparatus. Also at Xavier's urging, Honor would decide to appoint her brother as "Chief Administrator" of Norrhollow, a vague title with unclear responsibilities, which Xavier sees to use as a carte blanche for his own participation in the so-called Midnight Operations.

After holding a meeting with Vespertine Minister of Foreign Affairs Alice Ostman and Minister of Environment Mors Stillebrann, Xavier would receive "extraordinary approval" to form a rapid reaction force to quickly bring peace and order to Central Vespuria, formally merging the Norrhollow State Reserve, the Norrhollow Home Guard, and CAUSE into a single cohesive fighting force called the Separate Group of Forces (SGF), which was to operate in parallel to the Vespertine Armed Forces. Officially, troop numbers would be kept at just around 14,000 men, though in fact SGF numbers would actually swell to around 50,000 men, the bulk of them SummitONE and MROS Dynamics contractors which Xavier would secretly stuff into the SGF without formal government approval.

The rest of the government-owned military forces would not have publicly-known commanders, though perhaps to keep up pretenses the Separate Group of Forces would assert that their highest commanding officer was ultimately Honor Almstedt, though it was clear which Almstedt was controlling things from the backlines. CAUSE, meanwhile, is highly suspected to be under the joint leadership of Viva Ravnskald and Mors Stillebrann.

In any case, the Vespertine Separate Group of Forces would begin its long march out of Stormhaven and towards the Four Havens. Because of the chaotic mess that was still developing down south, Xavier would be hard at work contacting all available government agents still present, hoping to secure Midnight Operation contracts with as much magnates as possible, with the Board of Directors advising the SGF to prioritize contracts with the Ministry of Magic. CAUSE under Viva Ravnskald, on the other hand, is advised to reach out to the Holy See given CAUSE's decent track record with unconventional operations and its primarily Norric composition, making it far more well-versed in the arcane compared to other SGF forces.

Minister Alice Ostman, from her base of political power in Burrow, would also be contacted by Almstedt Corporation to shore up military units in the other northern Albic states. Though, given the weakness of her own political power since the establishment of the Vespertine monarchy, Ostman would make no assurances of success, and would send out field investigation teams to find anyone (or anything) that was willing to join on a suicide mission in defense of the homeland.[/quote]

[b]The Unlikely Ostman Miracle[/b]

You'd think one would not find such patriotism given recent borderline schizophrenic events of both the world and nation. Unfortunately the Albic, now Vespurian, had never been the most mentally apt or logical sort of folk. Bright, ingenious, avantgarde, and other things, sure, but above all, they're patriotic.

One had to just patriotically mention the homeland, and legions of mercenary and veterans militia rose up, springing like animals just out of winter hibernation. But what cemented the aid package was not just the Minister's investigators, but the woman who went out to arm them with spirit and arms too.

The Grand Princess Mary, seems, refused to hole up in a bunker and 'hope' she didn't get dragon roasted like the magnates that are now jumping at the seams to take any and every contract from that SGF. Through her father, the Emperor, she took executive command of Kingsmount and from there she strongarmed the nearby northern Albic states with her.

Ostman was just the unlikely thing she needed to seize opportunity.

Die for the magnates and some faraway government? Does not sound as inspiring as Dying for the Homeland. And die they would...not. The Grand Princess would take effect and care of abusing the deathless state of the nation to her advantage, whilst also seeking to remedy people's death. Some might not be saved. Most will.

Seeing the SGF heading southwest to Hyperion down the old Imperial Road, now a most perilous trek, the Emperor was quick to confirm the Almstedt administration of Norrhollow. Meanwhile similar orders were given to Hearth City and Avernus; bring forth legions worthy of Hyperion and march to the Heartland.

[b]Coordination, Countermeasures, Command[/b]

Vespurias remained in command of the defence of Hyperion. That was not a request for headlines, that was an operational fact. Civilians were told to stay away from the walls, to shelter, and to direct any noncombatant traffic to the marked havens.

Outside the southern wall, the Dark Horde still numbered roughly 500,000 combatants in the main vanguard, spread across five concentric assault camps and dozens of mobile raiding bands. They were visible at dawn as a ragged, dangerous ocean of banners, fires, mounted crews, and dark magics. Their siege lines had front density at the choke points, and they probed the walls nightly along three main sectors.

Thirty urban engineering battalions, plus local guild teams, ran continuous shifts repairing breach points, stacking rubble, widening parapets, and rebuilding collapsed scaffolds. Heavy scaffolds were erected at sectors 2 and 3 for rapid counterlift of ammunition and manpower. Truck convoys and electric lift platforms kept supply moving up the inner ramparts.

Meanwhile fortified emplacements hosted 120 long-barrel battery units, mag-augmented and crewed by artillery crews and magineers. Sniper belts were organized along rooftops and tower ledges, numbering 2,400 marksmen in shifts. Mobile anti-beast squads of 3,600 troopers were on call to push back mounted charges. Local militia added 18,000 sharps and short-range teams.

The Ministry of Magic, never idle, under Case Arcane protocols, set layered wards. Three concentric ward rings were erected: Field damp and null pockets at the outer glacis; active deflection arrays along the inner curtain; and emergency kill-runes installed at critical gatehouses. Stabilization cores, experimental units, were placed at nodes Alpha, Beta, Gamma, each run by combined teams of arcane engineers and military wardens. AMORS triage teams began phased reconnection, starting with node Alpha at 04:00, with a target partial sync in 18 hours and wider lattice rechecks in 72. The objective: blunt the worst of the raw surge, restore readouts, and give arcane crews the chance to push back uncontrolled emanations.

Meanwhile a reserve pool of 40,000 men stood under direct imperial command, drawn from professional units and vetted militia. Supply lines were routed to three inner depots. Ammunition, warding reagents, and medical packages were rationed and prioritized. No civilian vehicles were permitted inside the inner ring.

A single-sheet order was issued and broadcasted: register or be interdicted. Mercenary groups had four options: A, integrate under State contract and accept rules of engagement and payroll; B, operate as neutral contractors with monitored lanes and restricted zones; C, surrender heavy armaments and be resettled; D, leave. Contracted units would receive accredited pay, supplies, legal indemnity for combat acts under directive, and clear extraction windows. Noncompliance would be treated as hostile. Merc leaders had twelve hours to answer. Payment guarantees were backed by immediate escrow and the state promise of post-crisis arbitration. Nothing secret. Nothing optional.

Emperor Aurean I, for the first time since the city was sealed, left the inner palace. He wore no parade uniform. He wore field gray, a short cloak for the cold, and the Imperial Guard in two compact columns. The Emperor moved through the inner gate, walked the ramparts, met wardens, engineers, and crew chiefs. He signed orders on site. He placed a hand on a stabilization core console and approved a localized discharge to stop a small breach. He did not speak grand speeches. He asked if the men were fed, if medicines reached the second lines, asked the armorers when the next round would be ready. He was present. That presence shortened the queue of indecision. Soldiers heard him, and the staff moved faster because he had walked the walk. The Emperor's appearance was tactical, not theatrical.

AMORS reconnection, in short, was basically phased out into 3 with more optional phases should it be successful: Phase 1, immediate triage node Alpha, 18 hours partial sync. Phase 2, repair and stabilize peripheral farms, 72 hours expanding readouts. Phase 3, prioritized lattice stabilization for the White Tree perimeter, 5 days hard target. Each phase used paired teams: arcane engineers plus military escorts, with telemetry relays run by electric mag relays. They're with one goal for now. Buy time. Restore enough arcane telemetry to predict the worst surges. Harden the walls to an acceptable breaching threshold. Move the Dark Horde from mass siege into attrition. Keep mercenaries functioning under control. Keep the Emperor close enough to see the problem and far enough to be protected.

The Emperor was having strong very strong second guesses about the concept of monarchy and how much he didn't want to be involved with it. He severely missed his senator and governor days.

[b]The Siege, The Surge, The Second Thoughts[/b]

Hyperion became a funnel. Every northern banner seemed to be on the road south. First came the Kingsmount Host, 60,000 strong, led front and center by Grand Princess Mary, who refused to stay in the rear. Behind her rolled their artillery trains, heavy-chassis arcanist carts, airlift engines, with medical detachments feeding into the eastern triage districts. Then the Hearth Host, 40,000, mostly regulars and fire teams, set in disciplined blocks with strong signal routing staff. The Averne Host, 35,000, half-motorised, half-infantry, arrived last.

Mercenary hosts followed in their wake. Rough numbers estimated them at 70,000 in total, from small bands of 50 to whole outfits of 5,000, banded under watchful eyes at the outer screening fences. They came in heavy gear, most in hardened rigs or with talismanic armor, with strange banners and mixed languages. Neutral contractors wore armbands that marked status per the directive. Each step past the gates was monitored. Those who did not register remained beyond the third wall, and some simply chose to leave. But many stayed, drawn to the pay or the fight or both. The walls were crowded with rifles, storm runes, men, women, and standing room only.

And some 40 some agents from Chamor that looked straight out of Maverick.

The Emperor was present, and the pressure was visible. His face no longer bore that old idealism, it carried exhaustion, frustration, and a new question, something like was this worth it. A nation that was once a commonwealth, capable of electing and removing its architects, had become a crown, and the crown now had to stand in the freezing wind with the men that kept it upright. He looked over the parapet and watched the Dark Horde press. He wondered if senators would have handled this better. He wondered if this thing called monarchy had turned an ideal into a burden. He wondered if, should they win, a return to ballots and shared power would make more sense than wearing a title that weighed too heavy.

But time was not elastic, and the Dark Horde did not wait.

The assault began at the dusk of one of the latter days of October. The first wave was not living matter. It came as a sheet of raw arcane pressure. A dark surge, a physical fog that pressed itself into the warding lines and hammered the first ring. Three holes opened in the field-damp layers, and two dozen arcane anchors shattered. Then came the second wave: a barrage of catapulted necrotic projectiles, each one bursting into clustered bone spines and cursed mists. The third wave followed immediately, a mounted charge of twisted beasts; horned rhinos, ash-skinned direwolves, and undead cavalry who rode like they felt no pain, that is, until a rifle round hit them in the spine.

The walls answered with measured violence. Ward engineers slammed new anchors into place. Batteries fired mag-augmented munitions at the charging lines. Firelances lit up the forward slopes. Sniper belts targeted commanders and banner carriers. Anti-beast squads surged to the outer walkways, firing explosive granades into the creature heads. Above all, aerial wards came online and expelled the darkest of the magic. For every corridor that buckled, two were patched. Bodies stacked in storm light and dye smoke.

And AMORS was reconnecting.

Node Alpha, 75 percent sync. Telemetry feeds showed stable core breathing. A vast web of arcane readings started to flicker into life across half the city. Hospital towers began using the reconnect to stabilize magical slippage in the undead-afflicted. Elders and children in warded wards were receiving life-sustaining therapies before the density drop could kill them. Surgeons and priests stood side by side in medical pavilions while giant spell-wards saturated rooms with healing fields. The work was brutal, but it was working. Vespurias needed to end the siege before the clock marked the density collapse.

The Dark Horde pushed again. This wave carried flying monstrosities  rune-burned wyverns, skinless serpents with wings, floating masses of brain matter dripping black ichor. Aerial guardians rose up to intercept, runecarved strike gliders, combat mages on lift plates, and turreted quad-cannons that spat iron and binding arcana. Someone had the very bright idea of floating artillery before they figured the recoil would send the thing flying backwards into a building. Bodies, human, beast, airborne, fell to the fighting lights of artillery arcs. The night was lit with emerald, red, blue, white. Too much to name or narrate.

Then came the order.

The Emperor called for the gates to open.

Reserves were rallied. Arcane carriers pushed forward. Heavy infantry stood ready behind tower shields. Mercenary contingents willing to join were given green flares and paired to regular squads. The Emperor took center stair, walked before his soldiers, asked for a rifle, then pointed to the breach. He might be old and over two to three decades since he killed anybody but he sure as hell could aim.

He felt an odd sense of thrill about it, that washed over the tiredness of the crown.

The assault force, about 30,000 strong, charged into the broken southern corridor. The Dark Horde had banked too close, expecting a stand-fight. Instead, they met a wall of counter-surge. Battery fire cleared lanes. Wards pulsed into physical shockwaves. Engineer squads detonated prepared charges beneath hostile mass. The Emperor moved under escort, passing orders through signal teams. The push was not pretty. It was a grind. It was close combat in cursed mud and reinforced stone. But it drove the Horde back and it cut the leading bodies of their host.

The goal was not to win outright. The goal was to fracture momentum, break the siege focus, and stall the mass until AMORS sync finished and the next major counteroffensive could be launched. And it worked in part. The Dark Horde was forced back half a mile. Their lines were stretched, and command signals fractured.

By the dawn of the next day, October 27th, the Horde still stood, but not as one solid front. The fields were scarred with magical disruptions and burned bodies. The walls of Hyperion stood, cracked but standing. And AMORS? Node Alpha complete, Beta 30 percent, Gamma primed for link. The country began to feel the arcane stabilizers open veins of clarity. Magical healing flooded the triage domes. Field hospitals ran surgeries on soldiers whose wounds should have been fatal. For once, the convergence of magic and medicine did not break a law of nature. The medics got to use very uncanny methods of saving people since they couldn't die. Some perhaps too enthusiastically.

The Emperor sat in a war tent after, cloak slung, hair unkempt. He signed another casualty report, another logistics order, another request from a merc captain. His expression did not match that of a monarch in triumph. It matched a man submerged in endless responsibility. He looked at the names on the page. He thought, this was easier when we argued in senate chambers. This would have been shared if we were still a commonwealth. Maybe after this, after the horde breaks and the dead stop walking, maybe it is time to give the voice back. Maybe crowns were a mistake.

[b]The Battle of the Heartland[/b]

The dawn after the countercharge saw neither silence nor stalemate. Orders from the Imperial War Office clarified the new plan: break the vanguard, force a rout, and free the open land below Hyperion for maneuver warfare. The Dark Horde still held numerical superiority, around 450,000 after the night losses, but they had overextended forward to press the breach. That overextension gave Vespurias one thing they had not had in weeks: room.

Three host forces moved with purpose: Kingsmount held the west pincer, Hearth the center, Averne the east. Combined total: over 120,000 troops backed with armor, artillery, and airborne units. The Emperor ordered the break-out line to be drawn across a seven mile stretch of southern farmland, mostly treeline, fallow fields, and old irrigation canals. Air reconnaissance confirmed enemy massing clusters within those canals. That would be the first strike point.

Kingsmount deployed 88 Leopard 2A7s and supporting IFVs, spearheaded by Princess Mary's command carrier. Drone swarms guided by 12-person arcane signal crews marked enemy concentrations with a glowing blue tag in real time. Hearth followed with mechanized infantry, 4,000 men in Wolfhound APCs, supported by three batteries of M109 self-propelled howitzers. Averne sent out twin rotary wings of Z-20 transport helos and two squadrons of strike birds armed with HEAT rockets and incendiary payloads.

At 10:42, the first salvo hit. Eight HIMARS trucks fired their full load at the southern canal line, smashing clusters of undead cavalry and storage pits. In those pits were hundreds of grafted skin beasts and stitched wyverns that had been held for a second assault. The HIMARS wrecked seventy percent of them before they could launch. Fragmentation tore bodies and constructs apart. The air shimmered with loose magic, trying to pull the gore back together, but the stabilization wards laid earlier by Ministry of Magic field units blunted the rebound.

Under the cover of that chaos, Kingsmount armor advanced in wedge formation, turrets locked on forward silhouettes. Apex crews loaded thermobaric rounds to counter massed infantry. When the first wave of humanoid attackers broke from the haze, rifles and cannons opened up. They fell, some to fire, some to disintegration spells by the guild support teams mounted in escort trucks behind the third line.

AMORS telemetry during this was reaching 82 percent sync in Node Beta. Reports from hospitals in Hyperion's fourth district came in: Patient 775, full reversal of necrotic spreading; Patient 221, life function restored after twenty-seven minutes in magical suspension. The rate of "effective rescues" climbed into dozens per hour. Priests and surgeons worked in relay, diving between trauma mending and ritual cleansing. One of them, a tired-looking trauma medic, said to a priest, "We're holding them together better than the walls are holding back the Horde." Thankfully the media was keeping a constant flow of reports to keep morale alive.

Back on the field, Hearth troops secured a three-kilometer strip of orchard land. They laid razorwire and set up two forward operating aid stations. Mortar crews were instructed to hold fire unless the Dark Horde regrouped for a forward push. They did not have to wait long.

The Horde regrouped.

Near noon, a combined mass of 80,000 surged in two giant columns. One contained human-like infantry with crude armor, heavy melee weapons, and spell shields. The other was a malformed breakout of larger beasts, ogres in bone graft suits, rhino-stitched horrors with welded plates, and a giant skeletal frame powered by purple fire. That thing stood twenty meters, had no skin, and charged straight down the Averne line.

Averne's air support did not hesitate. The Z-20s broke into staggered wings, released rocket pods and flame canisters. Magic-reactive phosphor caught and clung to the monsters, and the skeletal giant buckled under repeated blasts. But not fast enough. Three of the Averne IFVs were crushed under that behemoth before an anti-armor team planted a shaped charge fueled with molten sigils that ripped the chest apart. The thing fell, but it screamed with more than lungs. The acoustic hit knocked helmets off and disabled radios for ten seconds.

The Dark Horde used the confusion. Their shaman units cast mass disorientation hexes to blind frontline sharps. But this was the Vespurian army, not unprepared militia. Commander Asher, Hearth line, gave the order: C-Teams, visor mode three, magic dampen, advance two hundred, stagger spacing, ready grenades. And they did. The helmets flickered, runes dampened the worst, and 2,000 men lobbed mag-aug grenades in a rolling boom that obliterated half of the incoming press.

At 13:20, AMORS Beta hit 95 percent, and Gamma linked to Alpha. Arcane bleed in the central tract began to drop. That meant one thing for field command: push while the magic was still active and concentrated. They had about a two-hour window before the arcane fields fell into predictable density waves.

The Emperor, from his reinforced field tent, relayed the order: all forward hosts, Forward-Defensive Timeline Phase Two, objective: sever the Horde's backline. The hosts moved. And this time, it was not just cannons and magic.

A coordinated airstrike came from above. Ten F-15Es, armed with JDAM smart bombs, moved in low altitude. Their targets: five command spires, identified by recon as the magical relay nodes the Horde was using to broadcast their orders. One by one, the bombs erased those spires. A column of black magic erupted from each hit, flickered, then died. The Dark Horde's formations faltered. Command lines buckled. They lost cohesion. Panic spread in some parts. Rage in others. But without control, rage is just noise.

And so it came. The final signal from the Emperor.

"Send them to hell."

Kingsmount tanks rolled to maximum speed and fired direct-cannon barrages into the broken lines. Hearth infantry advanced with flamethrowers and cutting beams. Averne mounted guns tore apart stragglers, while mercenary companies charged under flares, finishing routing pockets with bullet, fire, and spell.

By 16:30, the vanguard was no more. Around 80,000 of the Dark Horde lay dead or abandoned. Another 100,000 broke south in disorder. The rest fell back to the fourth line at half-strength. The siege of Hyperion was not broken yet, but the initiative had shifted.

AMORS Gamma sync hit 40 percent by nightfall. Healing crews did mass triage under temporary arcanum domes. One medic said that if they get the full sync, rhey can bring back 50 percent of those medically coded dead this morning. The Emperor stood beside a burning tank wreck, watching the wounded be lifted off stretchers by floating rune platforms. He looked at the carnage. He thought of elections and arguments, not orders and body counts. He wondered if power belonged to one man, or to many voices rising in debate and dissent.

But that was the thought of tomorrow. For now, the only thought was simple: finish this and kill the bastards.

[b]End of the Endless Night[/b]

The vanguard broke, then unraveled. What followed was not a glorious cavalry pursuit, but a hard, methodical hunt through fields, hedgerows, and ruined hamlets. Command issued that same night: no refugee shooting, capture if possible, burn only when necessary. That order slowed some units, but it kept the moral code intact and kept the healers from having to sort ash from living.

Casualty counts were tallied at dawn. Immediate losses on Vespuria side: 9,300 dead, 24,800 wounded, 3,200 missing. Enemy bodies numbered roughly 95,000 counted on the plain, burned or shattered. Another 140,000 fled south in broken columns. Numbers were estimates, but they were sufficient.

Operation Seal and Sweep began at 05:00.

Phase One, Contain: three blocking lines were established. Kingsmount forces held the western cordon with 30,000 troops, 40 tanks, and mobile anti-air batteries. Hearth controlled the center cordon with 25,000 troops and two artillery brigades, plus counter-magic teams. Averne took the eastern cordon with 30,000 troops and mechanized brigades. Mercenary companies filled gaps, screened flanks, and ran recon-in-force. Each cordon was 15 to 25 kilometers deep, with patrol bases every 6 kilometers. Drone coverage was near-continuous.

Phase Two, Hunt: small combined-arms teams of 800 to 1,200 men executed clearing ops along identified corridors. They used quad-cannons, pack flamers, and mag-aug shotguns to flush dens of beasts. Night raids used silent electric APCs and arcane damp grenades to prevent spontaneous resummoning. Capture teams brought in prisoners where possible for interrogation. Many captives were not human but animated constructs, stitched corpses, or thrall-laden villagers; those were routed to screening stations for Ministry handling.

AMORS progress continued. Node Gamma reached 78 percent by the second day; global telemetry linked 60 percent of peripheral farms. That gave field commanders a new tool: predictive surge maps. Using those, engineers could route patrols away from likely arcane spikes and shepherd civilians into safe lanes. Hospitals reported steady rates of stabilization. Triage domes moved from chaos to procedure. Surgeons performed field resuscitations with mag-assisted grafts and arc-sutures. The list of those saved grew hourly. Children, elders, and key personnel were prioritized.

Phase Three, Retake AMORS: Ministry teams, escorted by armored columns, pushed to retake damaged runestone farms. These were hard fights. The enemy used the farms as anchor points, not out of strategic sense but for ritual reasons. Retaking a farm required a mixed team: 150 infantry, 30 arc-techs, 6 engineers, a small artillery screen, and 2 merc squads. Once secure, engineers sealed fractures and installed temporary cores. Over five days, 18 peripheral farms were retaken and brought to 50 to 80 percent operational. Each retake produced a morale spike for surrounding towns.

Phase Four, Convert Attrition into Encirclement: instead of chasing every fleeing group, command funneled remnants toward the Pact-held coasts. Naval interdiction, along with forward fire from field artillery and airstrike harassment, channeled breaking enemy columns into predictable routes. The intention: deny escape into hinterlands and force them into pockets where local militia and Pact naval landing forces could interdict. By day seven, three major pockets were forming near the southern marsh corridor and two in the eastern lowlands. Although many of the airborne or more stronger beings simple fled or teleported away, having long since prepared to abandon the Dark Horde like a bad horse in a race, they took off like cockroaches into the wider planes of Erene.

Humanitarian push ran parallel. Mobile healing units, run by arc-medic teams and civilian surgeons, moved along cleared roads. Triage hubs processed thousands. Where an AMORS node was partial but usable, med teams applied stabilization wards long enough to perform complex surgeries: limb reattachment, necrotic excisions, and arc-cleansing. Field reports said 42 percent of those coded as near-fatal were returned to conscious function by day five. The clock was still tickingfull AMORS restoration remained the only guarantee against later deaths, but the combination of mag-med and surgery bought time and lives.

Supply and logistics were relentless. Ammunition flows used emergency bond funds. Electric convoy lines ran on prioritized charging hubs. Engineers improvised charging trailers for APCs using mag-cores borrowed from retaken farms. Food and clean water caravans ran escorted routes. The state kept strict rationing to avoid breakdowns.

By the last days the tempo changed. Enemy pockets had no central leadership left, or competent one at least, the smart ones had already fled the nation. Smaller groups tried to survive by improvisation: some looted, others attempted makeshift pacts with local brigands. Where they attempted to reorganize, local militias and town hosts, reinforced by garrisoned Imperial units, cut them down. The mop-up was brutal at times. Screening tribunals processed captured sorcerers; those found guilty of high ritual crimes received summary sentencing under Case Arcane protocols. Less of a firing squad and more of "We are LITERALLY sending you to hell" method of execution. Chiefly befsau half of these had some form of back up immortality or some other annoyance. The "the demon made me do it" didn't hold up in court for warlocks.

AMORS full sync reached a turning point on day eleven. With major lattice nodes at 92 percent and peripheral farms at 70 to 88 percent, arcane telemetry allowed nationwide scheduling. Surge teams worked in 6, 12, and 24 hour cycles to push remaining residual surges into controlled venting. When the White Tree perimeter stabilization registered 60 percent secure, the Ministry released a conditional easing: limit curfew adjustments for cleared zones, more field hospitals authorized, and accelerated safe extraction corridors for displaced civilians.

Encirclement operations succeeded in two key areas within 15 to 18 days. Pocket Alpha in the south contained roughly 35,000 enemy combatants; Pocket Beta in the east contained 22,000; smaller pockets totaled near 18,000. The strategy was containment, soften, and capture. Siege guns and arc-lances hammered hardened clusters. Psychological operations used captured ritualists to broadcast surrender offers. Many surrendered. Thousands fled into marshes and were cut off later.

The interior was under controlled combat. The Imperial line was mobile again, not merely defensive. Units were ordered to clear every village that reported infestation. Where residents had been thrall-linked, teams used cleansing rituals and medical wards. The pattern became standard: secure, cleanse, treat, rebuild. Mobile repair units fixed wells, re-energized small runestones for local wards, and installed temporary null rings to prevent reoccupation.

The final push toward the Pact coasts was a coordinated blockade. Naval forces took positions to deny escape at sea. Coastal batteries and Pact landing forces closed the funnel. The remaining enemy remnant strength was estimated at 42,000 across five pockets. Over the next hours, coordinated ground and naval attacks collapsed those pockets. Casualties on Vespuria side during mop-up were heavy in small skirmishes, but the overall toll was contained.

Engineers repaired bridges, medics ran long hours, and Ministry teams continued to purge corrupted runes. The Emperor, present in mop-up command and visibly hollowed, ordered a nationwide schedule: retake every AMORS node, rebuild municipal wards, and begin a layered restoration of civil institutions. He did not pretend the crown made this easier. It did not. But it had centralized a necessary response. That reality weighed on him.

[b]All Quiet After Midnight[/b]

October 31st came without ceremony, but it came. The fields outside Hyperion, once full of burning sigils, bodies, and siege crews, lay quiet. No storms of magic. No creature calls. Just the wind against broken fences and dug earth. The last encirclement pockets had fallen two days earlier. The final mop-up was done before dawn. Now the state moved into the most delicate part of any war: the counting, the cleaning, the keeping of promises made to the living and the dead.

The casualty reports began early. They were clinical, terse, signed by ministers and verified by automated tallies through AMORS sync. Total Vespurian military dead: 15,121 confirmed. Missing, presumed dead: 2,002. Civilians documented dead by direct result of combat or surge: 38,400. Civilian deaths from indirect causes, later healing complications, or rural collapse: 9,700. Total healed or saved from magical death states: 126,300. Of those, 41 percent required continued medical care. The remaining would live normally again. Some walked out of triage hospitals and into the arms of families who refused to believe the nightmare was done. Others were given a quiet hour in rooms surrounded by those they loved before the last of the stabilizing magic dissolved. They were not resuscitated. They were let go humanely, without screams or spells, only hands held and farewells spoken. A brief allure of immortality faded with gratitude instead of horror.

The Dark Horde left its own figures behind. Rough estimate of total combatants killed: 350,000. Captured: 47,000. Unaccounted: 15,000-20,000. The highest tier leaders, the strongest wielders of wild sorcery, did not fall in the mud. They fled. Some vanished in blinding pillars of spellcraft. Others simply rose on dragonback, wyvern wing, or teleportation flash. Where they fled, the state does not know. Where they will go, nobody dares to predict. Their threat is not gone, merely... "Out of Jurisdiction".

By midday, the imperial contingencies began to roll back. Case Arcane was suspended, not lifted. Emergency Courts closed their high tribunals. The War Council dissolved into interim reporting units. But the executive powers? Those stayed. The Emperor was required to maintain continuous authority until the full reconnection and stabilization of AMORS was declared complete by the Ministry and armed forces. Nobody argued. Nobody wanted another month like the last seven.

The White Tree, now unbound from the crisis, did not return to its old white-red style. It remained gold. Glowing gold, shapely, solid, and alive with a quiet hum that filled the capital without searing the eyes. AMORS showed that the arcane density had stabilized at roughly 18 percent above pre-event norms, still far below the lethal surge threshold. What that meant long-term, no one knew, but for now, it meant safety. It meant the sky stayed blue and did not divide in ribbons of spellfire.

News and media did what they always did: they made lists. Lists of dead, of saved, of heroes, of failures, of rumors. Children born during the siege were named things like Beacon, Bastion, Dawn. Everyone disliked that and one could already predict the incoming bullying in a decade to come. Newspapers printed photos of field meals being shared by Pact soldiers and Vespurian recovery crews. Old men cried openly during broadcasts. School teachers lit lanterns in classrooms and read the first official death-return reports aloud. Waffle House did not close throughout a single day in the crisis.

The Pact was asked officially the same evening: for humanitarian fuel convoys, medical supply packages (non-magical), reparative engineering crews, and shelter kits for displaced rural zones. No ceremonial pleas. Just logistics on a spreadsheet, signed by the Foreign Minister, stamped by the Emperor, mailed with a line that read Thank you in advance.

November 1st dawned gray and cold over Hyperion. The city woke slower than usual. A third of the population was asleep after 36-hour shifts. Children were silent on trams. Priests and medics walked the streets together. The Empire remained under emergency powers, calm and orderly. Not triumphant but at least functional. AMORS was 98 percent restored. Hospitals still full. Fires still being put out in the interior. Engineers still diving into half-collapsed runestone farms to lock down stray currents.

But the immediate danger was gone.

The dead had stopped rising.

The sky was clear.

The walls still stood.

People hugged strangers just to feel real again.

All Quiet After Midnight. The crisis was not forgotten, not yet healed, but it was no longer a crisis. Now it was a lesson, a scar, and a country that did not fall, thankfully, just as it began again.
